Operational Inbox to TMS Shipment Entry Agent

Bookings, rate confirmations and shipment updates arrive through shared inboxes and PDFs. Staff re-key references, dates, parties, commodities and charges into the TMS.

Setup$10,000–$21,500
Monthly$4,000–$10,000
Delivery8–14 weeks
Relationship12–24 months
01 · Problem

What is broken today?

Bookings, rate confirmations and shipment updates arrive through shared inboxes and PDFs. Staff re-key references, dates, parties, commodities and charges into the TMS.

Primary business measureData-entry minutes per shipment; booking errors; exception rate; time to TMS record
02 · Customer

Who are you solving this for?

Ideal buyer

Freight forwarder owner or operations manager

Domain and segment

Freight Forwarders & Brokers · Logistics

03 · Service

What exactly do you build?

Classify messages, extract shipment fields with source links, validate customers/locations/rates, create draft TMS records and route only exceptions for approval.

04 · Workflow

How the solution operates

Classify messages, extract shipment fields with source links, validate customers/locations/rates, create draft TMS records and route only exceptions for approval.

Evidence enters→Rules validate→ AI prepares action→Human approves exceptions→ Result is recorded
05 · Commercial model

How this becomes a paid engagement

Engagement model

Paid diagnostic → implementation → managed optimization retainer

Duration

8–14 weeks delivery · 12–24 months

Suggested price range $10,000–$21,500 setup, then $4,000–$10,000 monthly.
06 · Client acquisition

Where to find buyers and how to convince them

Where buyers are

LinkedIn: freight owners, operations managers, dispatch leads; freight association directories; CargoWise/TMS communities; DAT groups; Google Maps; Upwork

Sales difficulty

Easy · 2/5 difficulty

Paid-pilot hookShadow-process one week or 20 historical cases using Shared email, PDFs; compare cycle time, exceptions caught, reviewer edits and unsafe edge cases before any production write-back.
07 · Delivery

Inputs, integrations and technology

Inputs and integrations

Shared email, PDFs, TMS/CargoWise, customer master, rate tables, tracking and document store; typical stack: TMS/CargoWise, shared inbox, PDFs, tracking APIs, Google Sheets, CRM, OCR and exception routing

Likely stack

TMS/CargoWise, shared inbox, PDFs, tracking APIs, Google Sheets, CRM, OCR and exception routing

08 · Risk controls

What must not go wrong?

Human exception approval, customer/carrier confidentiality, rate controls, document accuracy and message audit trails.

Implementation principleKeep source evidence, validation rules, human approval for high-impact exceptions, audit logs and controlled system write-back.
